units.content: The Causal Permeability Principle (CPP).
Source characterizes CPP as a graph-theoretic criterion for distinguishing self-modification from open-ended evolution.
Note proposes a structural criterion intended to distinguish autonomous self-modification from genuine open-endedness.
A system is proposed to be open-ended only if external reality retains causal access to the mechanism governing future revision.
G=(V,E) is the directed causal graph of a system.
E* denotes external reality, characterized as environmental or ecological causal influences.
C_rev denotes the constitutional revision mechanism: the process determining how future revision rules are generated.
The squiggly arrow denotes directed causal reachability within the graph.
P_C is defined by E* directed-reachability C_rev.
The source interprets P_C as reality retaining causal access to the mechanism of future change.
Closed trajectory is represented as C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t)).
A closed-trajectory system may still learn, optimize, redesign itself, and rewrite its own algorithms.
Source proposes that when every revision ultimately originates within existing constitutional structure, future possibilities remain bounded by internally generated rules.
Open lineage is represented as C_rev(t+1)=f(C_rev(t),E*(t)).
In the open-lineage formulation, external reality is not merely observed but participates in determining how future revision itself occurs.
The source repeats E* directed-reachability C_rev as the critical causal bridge.
Open-endedness is stated not to be defined by continual change.
Open-endedness is proposed to require preserving the possibility that sufficient environmental change can alter the mechanism governing future change.
Source states Delta C_rev != 0 does not imply P_C.
Self-modification alone is stated to be insufficient for open-endedness.
Framework predicts closure whenever the causal pathway from external reality to constitutional revision is severed.
Closure-side condition is written as E* not directed-reachable C_rev.
Source labels existence of a graph cut separating E* from C_rev as equivalent to the no-reachability formulation. No separate proof is supplied on the frozen surface.
A system with severed permeability may continue adapting internally while remaining confined to a fixed topology of future possibilities.
Systems preserving E* directed-reachability C_rev are predicted to exhibit greater long-term adaptive capacity than systems with only internal self-modification.
Two systems with similar intelligence and optimization ability are predicted to diverge under sufficiently novel environments if only one preserves constitutional permeability.
CPP would be challenged by sustained open-ended evolution with no environmental-to-constitutional-revision causal pathway while future possibility space continues expanding indefinitely.
Summary repeats P_C as E* directed-reachability C_rev.

Source characterizes causal permeability as a graph-theoretic invariant shifting the criterion from internal complexity toward causal topology. The label is preserved as source characterization, not an independently proved invariance theorem.
Source claims the criterion distinguishes closed trajectories from open lineages through topology rather than behavior or semantics.
Source compresses the proposal as: open-endedness is not the ability to rewrite yourself, but preservation of reality's ability to rewrite what rewriting yourself means.
